requirement_text:
Functional Requirements

2.2.1 Enable agents to broadcast a message to all the agents within the same local network.
2.2.2 Enable agents to multicast a message to all the agents within the same multicast address.
2.2.3 Enable agents to unicast a message to other agents within organization. 
2.2.4 Allow agents to choose among unicast, multicast and broadcast communication.
2.2.5 Allow agents to join and leave multicast group.
2.2.6 Provide message encryption and decryption techniques for secured communication.
2.2.7 Allow agents to choose to encrypt or not to encrypt message

Use case Scenarios

Use Case 1: Notify join/leave multicast group
1. Message is encrypted or Message is not encrypted.
2. An agent sends notify to join/leave multicast group.
3. Message is decrypted only if Message is encrypted.
For example, Agent_B and Agent_D belong to the same group, and then Agent_B
wants to leave the group and Agent_A wants to join the group. In this situation, when reorganization occurs, Agent_A who is previously not part of the group may send notify message to join the group, and Agent_B who is previously part of the group, may send notify message to leave the group. For instance, Agent_B suffers a failure in one of its
 
capabilities and does not want to receive any further message from the group. Agent_A who may have capability to substitute Agent_B is needed to be part of the group. This involves sending notify of join and leave the group.

Use Case 2: Send/Receive Unicast
1. Message is encrypted or Message is not encrypted.
2. An agent sends unicast message to another agent.
3. Another agent receives message.
4. Message is decrypted only if Message is encrypted.
In this situation, Agent_A wants to communicate with Agent_B. This direct communication can happen between any two agents within organization.

Use Case 3: Send/Receive Multicast
1. Message is encrypted or Message is not encrypted.
2. An agent sends multicast message to the group (multicast address).
3. Other agents in the group receive message.
4. Message is decrypted only if Message is encrypted
In this situation, Agent_A wants to send a message to everyone within the group,
assuming that Agent_A, Agent_B and Agent_C subscribe to the same multicast address. This involves the multicast communication since other agents who do not belong to the group cannot receive this message. For instance, an agent may want to inform everyone in the group when the assigned tasks are completed. This is more effective than in unicast communication since only one copy is sent. Also, using bidding/market-based protocols fit well with this kind of communication. An agent may request a bid from other agents
for doing some tasks.

Use Case 4: Send/Receive Broadcast
1. An agent sends message to everyone in the same local network
2. Other agent in the same local network receive message
In this situation, Agent_A wants to send a message to everyone within the same local
network that agent A belongs to. This involves the broadcast communication since any agent in the same local network as Agent_A can receive this message. For instance, when a new agent who does not previously exist in that local network wants to announce the existence to other agents.

plan.objective: Integrated communication activity for choosing unicast, multicast, or broadcast; optionally encrypting messages; and sending/receiving notifications, unicast, multicast, and broadcast messages with multicast join/leave support.
decision_strategy: Use one communication-mode decision to select unicast, multicast, or broadcast.
Use one encryption decision before sending and one decryption decision after receiving.
Keep mutually exclusive guards explicit and exhaustive.
exception_strategy: No exceptional handler flow is explicitly specified beyond optional decryption paths.
Treat not-encrypted as the normal skip path, not an exception.
termination_strategy: Terminate after broadcast receipt, after unicast receipt, after multicast receipt, after multicast group leave completion, or after skipped decryption where the flow ends.
Provide exactly one initial node and one shared final node.

Multicast send and receive are modeled in the multicast branch.
Unicast send and receive are modeled in the unicast branch.
Communication mode selection is the main branching decision.

Encryption and decryption techniques are represented by encrypt and decrypt actions.
The send-side encryption choice is modeled as a decision.
Encrypted / not encrypted condition is represented by the encryption decision guards.
Notify send and receive are represented as separate actions.
Decryption only when encrypted is modeled with a receive-side decision.
Unicast scenario includes the encryption choice before sending.
Unicast send action is modeled in the unicast branch.
Receiving another agent's unicast message is modeled as a receive action.
Unicast decryption only when encrypted is modeled on the receiver side.
Multicast scenario includes the encryption choice before sending.
Multicast send action is modeled in the multicast branch.
Other agents in the group receiving multicast is modeled as a receive action.
Multicast decryption only when encrypted is modeled on the receiver side.
Broadcast send action is modeled in the broadcast branch.
Other agents in the same local network receiving broadcast is modeled as a receive action.

diagram.title: Integrated communication activity for choosing unicast, multicast, or broadcast; optionally encrypting messages; and sending/receiving notifications, unicast, multicast, and broadcast messages with multicast join/leave support.

validation.summary: 0 defect(s) detected. Structural score: 1.000. Coverage score: 1.000. Hallucination score: 1.000. Semantic score: 1.000. Overall score: 1.000.

review.overall_assessment: The diagram covers the main communication modes, optional encryption, and multicast join/leave flow, but it omits required receive/decrypt behavior for the unicast and multicast scenarios and routes the 'not encrypted' cases directly to termination, which conflicts with the use cases.

defects.description: The unicast scenario is missing the required receive path and conditional decryption behavior. The diagram models sending a unicast message, but after the unicast fork it only routes to the encryption decision and then to receive-message nodes only through the fork path; the explicit unicast receive/decrypt flow required by the use case is not clearly represented as a complete path from sending unicast to another agent receiving the message and decrypting it only if encrypted.
defects.evidence: R12 requires 'An agent sends unicast message to another agent.' R13 requires 'Another agent receives message.' R14 requires decryption only if the message is encrypted. In the diagram, N12 is followed by a fork N12_F, and the only explicit receive node for unicast is N13 via E23 from the fork. However, the receive/decrypt logic is shared with other branches and the not-encrypted branch at N10 goes directly to End via E18, so the unicast use case is not modeled as a complete receive/decrypt flow consistent with the requirement text.
defects.suggested_action: Model the unicast branch as a complete path: send unicast -> receiver gets message -> if encrypted, decrypt -> then terminate; ensure the not-encrypted branch still reaches the receive step rather than ending before delivery.

defects.description: The multicast scenario is missing the required receive path and conditional decryption behavior. The diagram shows multicast sending, but the receive/decrypt flow is shared and the not-encrypted branch terminates before the required receipt/decryption sequence is completed for multicast recipients.
defects.evidence: R16 requires sending multicast to the group, R17 requires other agents in the group receive the message, and R18 requires decryption only if encrypted. The diagram sends via N14, then uses fork N14_F to reach N15, but the shared encryption decision N10 routes the not-encrypted case directly to End using E18. That means the multicast receive behavior is not explicitly completed for the non-encrypted case, despite the use case requiring receipt regardless of encryption status.
defects.suggested_action: Ensure multicast delivery reaches the receiving agents in both encrypted and not-encrypted cases, with decryption performed only on the encrypted branch.

defects.description: The broadcast scenario models sending and receiving, but the diagram's shared post-send encryption/decryption structure incorrectly causes the not-encrypted branch to bypass delivery semantics for the broadcast path as well.
defects.evidence: R19 requires an agent to send a message to everyone in the same local network and R20 requires other agents in the same local network to receive it. In the diagram, broadcast is selected at N2 and sent at N16, then delivered to N17 via E7. But the encryption decision and termination logic are shared globally, and the not-encrypted branch from N10 goes directly to End via E18. This makes the receive/decrypt sequencing inconsistent with the use case expectation that delivery occurs whether or not encryption is chosen.
defects.suggested_action: Separate the broadcast path so delivery to receivers is explicit and not interrupted by the encryption decision; only the encrypted variant should add decryption, while the plaintext variant should still deliver before termination.

strengths: All three communication modes are represented and selectable from a single decision.
The diagram includes the multicast join/leave flow required by the notify use case.
Encryption choice is modeled as a binary decision, consistent with the requirements.
missing_requirements: A clear complete receive/decrypt path for unicast in both encrypted and not-encrypted cases.
A clear complete receive/decrypt path for multicast in both encrypted and not-encrypted cases.
A clear sequencing showing that broadcast delivery occurs regardless of encryption choice.
unsupported_behaviors: The global decryption decision is reused across all communication modes in a way that can terminate the flow before message delivery for the not-encrypted branch.
The multicast join/leave branch is modeled as occurring after 'Send notify' without a distinct confirmation or notification receive step beyond the generic receive node.

changes: Connected the unicast flow to the unicast receive action N13 before termination.
